question: How do drugs primarily work inside the human body?

options.A: They alter existing biological processes.
options.B: They create entirely new cellular functions.
options.C: They replace missing body organs permanently.
options.D: They destroy all pathogens without exception.

explanation: Think of medicines as assistants, not inventors! They don't create brand new body functions; they simply speed up or slow down things your body is already doing naturally. You've got this! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is considered the gold-standard, first-choice treatment for chronic insomnia?

options.A: High-dose benzodiazepines every night
options.B: Complete sensory deprivation therapy
options.C: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I)
options.D: Over-the-counter antihistamines

explanation: CBT-I is the top recommendation! It helps retrain your brain and sleep habits for long-term success without any risk of drug dependence. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h8)

question: What is the clinical term for a fever or high body temperature?

options.A: Anoxia
options.B: Pyrexia
options.C: Hyperemia
options.D: Hypothermia

explanation: Spot on! Pyrexia is simply the medical word for a fever when your body's thermostat is temporarily turned up. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T6#GNS123_U3_T6_h2)

question: What form of the malaria parasite does a mosquito first inject into a person?

options.A: Merozoites
options.B: Gametocytes
options.C: Zygotes
options.D: Sporozoites

explanation: Correct! Infected mosquitoes carry sporozoites in their salivary glands and inject them right into your skin and blood when they bite. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which sign shows that the body can no longer compensate for blood loss?

options.A: A slow and steady decrease in heart rate
options.B: An increase in urine output by the kidneys
options.C: A sharp and sudden drop in blood pressure
options.D: A sudden return of normal skin color

explanation: When compensation fails, the blood pressure crashes. Recognizing this shift is a key nursing skill! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why do healthcare planners conduct a community needs assessment before setting up PAC services?

options.A: To recruit international doctors for specialized surgeries
options.B: To penalize traditional healers practicing in the village
options.C: To understand local barriers, health data, and access challenges
options.D: To determine the exact cost of medical equipment imports

explanation: A needs assessment helps us see what real-life factors delay care in the community—like transport issues or cultural fears—so we can design services that truly help people. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h2)

question: What happens if a standard ORS packet is mixed with way too little water?

options.A: It tastes better and is easier for babies to swallow
options.B: It creates a hypertonic solution that worsens dehydration
options.C: It neutralizes stomach acid more rapidly
options.D: It becomes more effective at curing the infection

explanation: If there's too little water, the mixture becomes too salty and concentrated, actually pulling more water out of the body's tissues into the gut! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T18#GNS215_U6_T18_h4)

question: What is the name for the surgical opening of the large intestine onto the belly wall?

options.A: A catheter
options.B: A stoma
options.C: An incision
options.D: A fistula

explanation: Great job! A stoma is simply the surgically created opening of the bowel onto the tummy surface where waste leaves the body. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h1)

question: A pregnant woman at 38 weeks gestation has a single baby lying head-down and normal blood pressure. Is she a candidate for home delivery?

options.A: Only if she refuses to take routine blood tests
options.B: Only if she has given birth five times before
options.C: Yes, she meets the basic criteria for a low-risk pregnancy
options.D: No, all women must deliver in a tertiary hospital

explanation: Her gestational age, singleton status, cephalic presentation, and normal vitals match the exact profile of a low-risk home birth candidate. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h3)

question: How do fontanelles help protect an infant's brain during early childhood?

options.A: By acting as shock absorbers and allowing room for the brain to expand
options.B: By keeping the inner ear bones aligned during early feeding
options.C: By sealing tightly to prevent blood from pooling under the scalp
options.D: By producing extra cerebrospinal fluid to nourish the growing brain

explanation: Exactly! They act like mini shock absorbers against bumps and give the rapidly growing brain all the space it needs. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T12#GNS121_U6_T12_h3)

question: As a student nurse, which action best supports a patient receiving end-of-life palliative care?

options.A: Focusing strictly on lab results rather than emotional needs
options.B: Listening openly to their fears and helping them find personal meaning
options.C: Telling them not to worry about dying and changing the subject
options.D: Restricting family visits to keep the patient completely isolated

explanation: Being a compassionate listener and validating a patient's feelings offers immense comfort during their final days. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h6)

question: Why are narrow-spectrum antibiotics preferred when you know the exact germ causing the trouble?

options.A: They work much faster than broad-spectrum drugs
options.B: They never cause allergic reactions in patients
options.C: They can be taken without water
options.D: They cause less harm to normal body flora

explanation: Spot on! Narrow-spectrum is like a sniper rifle—it hits only the bad bug and leaves your healthy friendly bacteria alone. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T2#GNS215_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which muscle action is responsible for moving waste along the colon?

options.A: Hemolysis
options.B: Peristalsis
options.C: Perfusion
options.D: Osmosis

explanation: Peristalsis refers to the wave-like muscular contractions that push food and waste steadily through the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is training local mothers as peer educators so effective in stopping harmful food taboos?

options.A: Mothers are legally required by the state to teach nutrition classes
options.B: Peer educators have advanced university degrees in clinical medicine
options.C: Mothers listen to fellow community peers who share similar daily life experiences
options.D: Peer educators receive a high monthly salary from international donors

explanation: People are much more likely to adopt new health habits when taught by trusted neighbors from their own background rather than outsiders. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h8)

question: What is the best approach for a nurse who wants to explore a patient's spiritual needs?

options.A: Wait until the patient experiences a severe medical crisis
options.B: Directly debate their personal religious practices for accuracy
options.C: Hand them a strict theological questionnaire to complete in silence
options.D: Ask gentle, open-ended questions about what brings them comfort and hope

explanation: Open questions let patients share what matters most in their own words, without feeling pressured or judged. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h4)

question: Why is supporting family caregivers considered such a vital part of home healthcare?

options.A: To prevent caregiver burnout and maintain safe care at home
options.B: Because family members replace the doctor in writing prescriptions
options.C: To ensure the family pays for all medical supplies out of pocket
options.D: Because nurses are not allowed to visit patients alone

explanation: Caring for a sick relative is exhausting. By supporting family caregivers, we protect their health and ensure they can keep providing safe care at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h8)

question: While checking a patient with a leg infection, you notice their toes are cool, pale, and slow to refill with blood. What is your best first move?

options.A: Apply a heating pad directly to the toes
options.B: Document the findings as normal post-surgical swelling
options.C: Encourage the patient to get out of bed and walk
options.D: Report the neurovascular changes to the physician immediately

explanation: Cool, pale toes with a sluggish refill mean blood flow is in trouble (or compartment syndrome is setting in). Always report this to the doctor right away! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h8)

question: Which part of the nervous system includes the sensory nerves branching out to your skin and organs?

options.A: Central nervous system
options.B: Peripheral nervous system
options.C: Autonomic sympathetic chain
options.D: Enteric digestive network

explanation: You got it! Think of the central nervous system as the main office (brain and spinal cord), while the peripheral nervous system is the field crew reaching out to every corner of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h1)

question: Why do nurses listen with a stethoscope before pressing or tapping on a patient's abdomen?

options.A: To follow hospital rules without any clinical reason
options.B: To make the patient feel more comfortable and relaxed
options.C: To prevent altering natural bowel sounds before listening
options.D: To ensure the procedure takes as little time as possible

explanation: Spot on! Pressing or tapping too early wakes up the tummy and makes sounds that weren't there originally. Always listen first! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h1)

question: How many weeks of pregnancy make up a normal term delivery?

options.A: Between 37 and 42 completed weeks
options.B: Between 28 and 34 completed weeks
options.C: Between 32 and 36 completed weeks
options.D: Exactly 40 completed weeks only

explanation: You've got this! A pregnancy is considered full term when it reaches anywhere from 37 up to 42 completed weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T004#GNS226_U3_T004_h1)

question: What is a primary tool used by nurses to record daily immunizations at the clinic level?

options.A: Patient financial billing receipts
options.B: Pharmacy drug manufacturing manuals
options.C: Immunization registers and tally sheets
options.D: Surgical theater operation logs

explanation: Tally sheets and registers are standard tools nurses use every day to keep a precise count of every vaccine given. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h8)

question: How do civil service rules and professional nursing acts work together for a public sector nurse?

options.A: Civil service rules completely replace professional nursing laws upon employment
options.B: The nurse must obey both administrative civil service rules and professional health regulations
options.C: The constitution prevents nurses from being held accountable to civil service guidelines
options.D: Professional council regulations only apply to private hospital nursing staff

explanation: As a public sector nurse, you answer to two bosses in a way: your administrative employers (civil service rules) and your profession (the nursing council). [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h2)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to ask about oral and anal sexual practices during a check-up?

options.A: Clients expect nurses to document their personal lifestyle choices for insurance
options.B: Urethral swabs are sensitive enough to detect infections in all other body parts
options.C: Infections can transmit across different mucosal sites and require site-specific testing
options.D: Standard blood tests will automatically cover all anatomical exposure sites

explanation: Germs don't just stay in the genitals! If a patient had oral or anal exposure, we need swabs from the throat or rectum to catch the infection accurately. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h4)

question: When is it legally okay for a nurse to share a patient's private medical diagnosis with someone else?

options.A: When a curious neighbor asks about the patient's illness.
options.B: When the nurse wants to discuss interesting cases on social media.
options.C: When the hospital manager asks casually out of curiosity.
options.D: When required by statute or public health laws for specific diseases.

explanation: Patient confidentiality is sacred, but the law allows exceptions when reporting public health threats (like certain infectious diseases or gunshot wounds) to the appropriate authorities. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of triage during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: To distribute financial relief funds to displaced families
options.B: To sort patients based on injury severity to prioritize critical care
options.C: To register patients for national health insurance policies
options.D: To assess structural damage to hospital buildings

explanation: Triage lets nurses and doctors quickly assess victims so that those with life-threatening injuries get treated first. You'll master this in clinicals! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h8)

question: How does benzonatate work to stop a patient's cough?

options.A: Anesthetizing stretch receptors in the respiratory tract
options.B: Depressing the heart rate to lower blood pressure
options.C: Paralyzing the muscles of the abdominal wall
options.D: Blocking histamine receptors in the nasal passages

explanation: Benzonatate acts locally by gently numbing the stretch receptors in the airways, stopping the urge to cough right at the source. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T1#GNS223_U2_T1_h2)

question: What exactly is a perineal laceration when a woman is giving birth?

options.A: A natural tear of the tissues between the vagina and anus
options.B: A rupture of the uterus during the second stage of labour
options.C: A surgical cut made by a doctor to widen the birth canal
options.D: A tear of the inner lining of the upper uterine cavity

explanation: Think of a perineal laceration as a natural tear that happens when the baby passes through. This is different from an episiotomy, which is a deliberate surgical cut made by the midwife or doctor. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h1)

question: Why is consistency in data collection so important during the empirical phase?

options.A: It guarantees that every participant will receive financial payment
options.B: It allows researchers to finish their shifts earlier in the day
options.C: It stops patients from asking questions about their treatment
options.D: It prevents errors and ensures measurements are reliable across all participants

explanation: If data is gathered differently for each person, the final results will be skewed and untrustworthy. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h5)

question: When an adverse event happens, what is the main goal of using 'systems thinking'?

options.A: Focusing entirely on disciplining the nurse who made the final error
options.B: Reducing the number of nursing staff on duty during night shifts
options.C: Moving away from blaming individuals toward fixing workflow processes
options.D: Assuming that technology can completely eliminate all human mistakes

explanation: Systems thinking stops the blame game. Instead of pointing fingers at a colleague, it looks at the environment and structural issues that allowed the error to happen in the first place. [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h3)

question: A nurse is checking a patient with early liver failure for brain confusion. Which physical sign should she look for?

options.A: Sudden paralysis of the lower extremities
options.B: Involuntary flapping tremor of the hands (asterixis)
options.C: Rigid muscle spasms in the jaw
options.D: Inability to focus the eyes on bright objects

explanation: Asterixis (often called a 'liver flap') is a classic sign where the patient holds their hands out, and the wrists briefly flap downward due to toxin buildup. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a general physical examination?

options.A: To diagnose complex psychiatric disorders independently
options.B: To replace the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.C: To prescribe appropriate pharmacological interventions
options.D: To gather baseline data about a patient's health status

explanation: A general exam is primarily done to establish a baseline of physical health so nurses can track changes over time. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h1)

question: What technology does an autoclave use to sterilize medical instruments and waste?

options.A: Pressurized steam
options.B: Dry microwave heat
options.C: Freezing temperatures
options.D: Ultraviolet rays

explanation: Autoclaves use high heat and pressure generated by steam to destroy all microbial life on equipment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h5)

question: What is the main goal of teaching a community about choking prevention?

options.A: To eliminate the sale of all round food items in local grocery stores
options.B: To ensure families purchase expensive medical safety equipment
options.C: To train every citizen to perform complex surgical procedures at home
options.D: To empower caregivers with knowledge to prevent incidents before they occur

explanation: Exactly! Teaching families how to spot risks and fix food shapes helps stop emergencies before they even start. Prevention is our best tool! [learn more](GNS324_U6_T7#GNS324_U6_T7_h6)

question: What substance must team up with vitamin B12 in the stomach so it can be absorbed properly in the lower small intestine?

options.A: Hydrochloric acid
options.B: Pancreatic lipase
options.C: Intrinsic factor
options.D: Bile salts

explanation: You got it! Stomach parietal cells secrete intrinsic factor, which binds to B12 like a VIP pass so the terminal ileum can safely absorb it. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T012#GNS227_U1_T012_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of emergency nursing when managing a life-threatening condition?

options.A: Conducting routine diagnostic laboratory tests
options.B: Completing a full health history before acting
options.C: Discharging the patient as quickly as possible
options.D: Rapid identification and immediate intervention

explanation: Emergency nursing focuses on acting fast to save lives when a patient's condition can quickly deteriorate. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the main job of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) in the kidneys?

options.A: Stimulating the excretion of excess water in urine
options.B: Blocking the reabsorption of sodium ions
options.C: Promoting water reabsorption into the blood
options.D: Increasing the production of red blood cells

explanation: Think of ADH as your body's water-saver. When you're running low on fluids, ADH tells your kidneys to hold onto water and put it back into your bloodstream. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is knowing research classifications important for evidence-based nursing?

options.A: It removes the need to talk directly with patients
options.B: It guarantees that hospital budgets will increase
options.C: It forces nurses to memorize difficult medical terminology
options.D: It helps nurses judge the strength and quality of evidence

explanation: That's right! Understanding how studies are grouped lets nurses evaluate whether a piece of evidence is strong enough to safely change patient care. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is a great community-level nursing action to help manage stress?

options.A: Closing down local markets to reduce neighborhood noise
options.B: Organizing mental health awareness campaigns and support groups
options.C: Prescribing strong antidepressant medications to every adult
options.D: Isolating stressed individuals inside regional hospitals

explanation: As community nurses, we shine brightest when we educate the public and create safe spaces where people can share and support one another. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h7)

question: What is the most common cause of rectovaginal fistula in developing countries?

options.A: Bladder stones
options.B: Hormonal imbalances
options.C: Chronic appendicitis
options.D: Prolonged and obstructed labor

explanation: Prolonged pressure from the baby's head against the pelvis causes tissue ischemia and necrosis, leading to fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: How do multidisciplinary ward rounds help improve rational drug use?

options.A: They eliminate the need for keeping written patient medical records
options.B: They reduce the number of patients admitted to the emergency department
options.C: Doctors, nurses, and pharmacists review drug necessity together to catch errors early
options.D: They allow nurses to bypass doctors and prescribe medications independently

explanation: Collaboration across disciplines brings different perspectives together, ensuring safer and more rational medication orders. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h7)

question: What does a bulging anterior fontanelle usually mean in a newborn?

options.A: Normal developmental closure
options.B: Severe systemic dehydration
options.C: Premature fusion of the skull
options.D: Increased intracranial pressure

explanation: Spot on! Extra pressure inside the head pushes the soft membrane outward, causing that tight, bulging feel. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h4)

question: Where does radioactive hospital waste usually come from?

options.A: Nuclear medicine and radiotherapy units
options.B: Administrative records and billing offices
options.C: General outpatient consulting rooms
options.D: Hospital kitchens and dining areas

explanation: Right on target! Radioactive materials are strictly used in specialized departments like cancer treatment and imaging. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which clinical condition is most likely to produce a weak, thready pulse?

options.A: Severe dehydration and fluid loss
options.B: Heavy physical exercise at the gym
options.C: Sudden fright or emotional excitement
options.D: Mild fever from a viral throat infection

explanation: Dehydration lowers blood volume, resulting in a weak, thready pulse that is difficult to feel clearly. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h5)

question: What kind of surgery involves removing a healthy organ because a patient has a high genetic risk of getting cancer there later?

options.A: Curative surgery
options.B: Prophylactic surgery
options.C: Diagnostic surgery
options.D: Palliative surgery

explanation: Great thinking! Prophylactic means preventative. Doctors perform this to remove healthy tissue before cancer ever gets a chance to start. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct cause of haemorrhage?

options.A: A ruptured internal aneurysm
options.B: A deep knife wound to the thigh
options.C: A bleeding stomach ulcer
options.D: Excessive red blood cell production

explanation: Having too many red blood cells (polycythemia) thickens the blood or increases volume, but it does not directly cause bleeding like a ruptured vessel or wound does. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h4)

question: How do screen-readers and talking appliances primarily help a visually impaired patient?

options.A: By physically guiding the patient's hands across household objects
options.B: By curing the underlying disease causing progressive blindness
options.C: By translating digital text and operational cues into audio feedback
options.D: By directly improving the optical clarity of damaged retinal tissues

explanation: Technology is amazing! When eyes need a break or can't see, turning text and appliance settings into spoken audio lets patients stay independent and in control. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T8#GNS311_U3_T8_h3)

question: What is a major long-term health complication frequently managed by nurses in patients who have undergone child marriage and early pregnancy?

options.A: Accelerated bone mineralization and high density
options.B: Permanent blindness caused by vitamin deficiency
options.C: Obstetric fistula and severe pelvic floor damage
options.D: Chronic respiratory infections from cold weather

explanation: Underdeveloped pelvises in young mothers often lead to obstructed labor, resulting in severe complications like obstetric fistula. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is the proper way to cut fingernails during routine care?

options.A: In a rounded shape with deep side corners
options.B: As short as possible down to the quick
options.C: In a deep V-shape to expose the nail bed
options.D: Straight across following the natural curve

explanation: Great thinking! Cutting straight across and avoiding digging into the corners helps protect your patient from painful ingrown nails. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h5)

question: What happens during catabolism in the human body?

options.A: Body fat is created from excess dietary sugars.
options.B: Complex molecules are broken down to release energy.
options.C: Simple amino acids are joined to form large muscles.
options.D: Nutrients are absorbed through the intestinal wall.

explanation: Catabolism tears big molecules down into smaller pieces to release quick energy for your body to use. You're mastering metabolism! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h6)

question: At what point should a sharps disposal container be closed and replaced to keep everyone safe?

options.A: One-quarter full
options.B: Halfway full
options.C: Completely filled to the brim
options.D: Three-quarters full

explanation: Never overfill a sharps bin! Closing it when it's three-quarters full ensures protruding needles won't accidentally prick anyone. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h7)

question: Administering post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to a recent survivor of sexual assault falls under which level of prevention?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Quaternary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: Secondary prevention involves immediate medical interventions after exposure to prevent long-term harm like disease transmission. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h4)

question: What do we call the process where cancer cells break away and spread through the blood or lymph to other parts of the body?

options.A: Mitosis
options.B: Metastasis
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Apoptosis

explanation: You're doing great! Metastasis happens when malignant cells travel via blood or lymph to set up secondary growths in distant organs. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the term for giving a patient too many different medications than they actually need?

options.A: Polypharmacy
options.B: Placebo therapy
options.C: Prophylaxis
options.D: Pharmacovigilance

explanation: Good job! Polypharmacy means 'many drugs' and happens when patients take multiple medications at once, increasing the risk of side effects. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which bleeding pattern is a serious warning sign (red flag) after a medical abortion?

options.A: Passing a single clot the size of a coin
options.B: Spotting that lasts for up to three weeks
options.C: Bleeding that stops completely after 24 hours
options.D: Soaking through two large pads per hour for two hours

explanation: You're doing great! Soaking through two large pads every hour for two hours straight is too much—it's a red flag that needs prompt medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h6)

question: An elderly patient taking many unnecessary drugs is most at risk for which problem?

options.A: Rapid increase in daily physical activity
options.B: Sudden improvement in physical endurance
options.C: Severe adverse drug reactions and toxicity
options.D: Complete immunity to all common infections

explanation: Older adults process drugs more slowly, making them highly vulnerable to side effects and dangerous drug interactions. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which federal Nigerian law makes female genital Mutilation a crime across the entire country?

options.A: The National Health Insurance Scheme Act
options.B: The Criminal Code Protection Act for Minors
options.C: The Nurses and Midwives Registration Act
options.D: The Violence Against Persons Prohibition Act

explanation: Correct! The VAPP Act (2015) is the key federal law in Nigeria that makes FGM a punishable criminal offense. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T5#GNS225_U6_T5_h3)

question: In health research, what is the standard benchmark usually accepted for statistical power?
explanation: Good memory! A power of 0.80 means your study has an 80% chance of catching a real treatment effect if it's actually there. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T17#GNS224_U1_T17_h6)

question: Which feature is most characteristic of a quantitative research study?

options.A: Statistical analysis and measurement
options.B: Detailed personal stories and interviews
options.C: Focus only on historical events
options.D: Absence of any numerical data

explanation: Quantitative research deals with numbers, variables, and measurable outcomes to test hypotheses. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why are IEC materials so important in primary health care?

options.A: They help bridge the gap between medical science and daily community practices.
options.B: They guarantee that patients will never contract infectious diseases.
options.C: They completely replace the need for physical clinical examinations.
options.D: They are primarily used by doctors to write medical prescriptions.

explanation: You'll use IEC tools all the time to translate big medical terms into simple, relatable ideas that everyday people can easily use at home. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h1)

question: What is the most common and clear sign that a patient has a kidney injury?

options.A: Severe swelling of both legs
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.C: Inability to pass any stool
options.D: Blood in the urine

explanation: Seeing blood in the urine (medical name: hematuria) is the classic red flag that tells us the kidneys have taken a hit. Always watch out for this in trauma cases! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h2)

question: What is a crucial hygiene rule to teach a patient recovering from middle ear surgery?

options.A: Keep water out of the operated ear canal
options.B: Allow shower water to enter freely to clean the area
options.C: Clean deep inside the ear daily with cotton buds
options.D: Irrigate the ear canal with warm tap water twice daily

explanation: Correct! Keeping the healing ear bone dry is essential to stop germs from getting in and causing an infection while the surgical site closes up. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h8)

question: What blood product is typically given to replace lost oxygen-carrying capacity in a massive haemorrhage?

options.A: Normal saline solution
options.B: Albumin protein liquid

question: What technology does flow cytometry use to help diagnose conditions like leukaemia?

question: Why is taking folic acid very important in the early months of pregnancy?

question: Why is peer support valuable for a patient who is newly disabled?

question: Why do patients with severe anxiety often complain of dry mouth and stomach upset?

question: A nurse manager wants to involve an experienced team of senior nurses in designing a new shift roster. Which style is best?

question: Which two brain chemicals are mainly responsible for balancing excitation and inhibition?

question: Why should nurses care about the mental health of patients with visible skin problems?

options.A: Depression automatically cures the skin condition
options.B: Mental distress stops creams from absorbing
options.C: Psychological issues prevent any infections
options.D: Emotional stress can worsen physical skin flare-ups

explanation: Great thinking! The mind and skin are closely linked, so stress and anxiety can actually make skin rashes worse. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T11#GNS213_U5_T11_h4)

question: What is the main job of von Willebrand factor in the body?

options.A: To help platelets adhere to injured vessel walls and carry factor VIII
options.B: To break down excess fibrin clots during tissue repair
options.C: To stimulate red blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.D: To constrict smooth muscle in damaged blood vessels

explanation: Von Willebrand factor acts like super-glue and a taxi! It helps platelets stick to the injury site and safely carries clotting factor VIII through the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why must sterile fields and items always be kept above waist level?

options.A: Hospital policies dictate that lower shelves are for waste
options.B: Gravity pulls heavier dust particles upward toward the chest
options.C: It prevents back strain during prolonged surgical procedures
options.D: Items below the waist are out of the nurse's direct line of sight

explanation: Anything below the waist or out of vision cannot be reliably monitored for contamination, so it is treated as unsterile. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h3)

question: What details should you write down in the chart after doing passive range of motion exercises?

options.A: The brand name of soap used for their bath
options.B: The patient's favorite food and religious beliefs
options.C: The cost of the hospital bed and your home address
options.D: Joints exercised, how the patient tolerated it, and any unusual findings

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing notes always focus on the clinical facts: what you moved, how they reacted, and anything out of the ordinary. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why do we encourage skin-to-skin contact right after a normal delivery?

options.A: It completely prevents the mother from experiencing postpartum bleeding
options.B: It speeds up the surgical healing of an episiotomy wound
options.C: It acts as a permanent immunization against childhood illnesses
options.D: It helps regulate the newborn's body temperature and encourages breastfeeding

explanation: That's right! Mum's body heat keeps the baby warm, and it gets breastfeeding off to a great start. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T15#GNS324_U5_T15_h4)

question: Which type of transport needs cellular energy (ATP) to move nutrients against a concentration gradient?

options.A: Simple diffusion
options.B: Osmosis
options.C: Facilitated diffusion
options.D: Active transport

explanation: Spot on! When the body needs to push substances 'uphill' against a gradient, it has to spend energy (ATP)—hence the name active transport. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T012#GNS227_U1_T012_h3)

question: What is the main way we define gender-based violence (GBV)?

options.A: Harmful acts based on sex or gender identity
options.B: Violent crimes committed exclusively against adult males
options.C: Accidental domestic injuries occurring at home
options.D: Physical injuries sustained during a street fight

explanation: GBV happens because of a person's sex or gender roles, rather than just random bad luck or street crime. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h1)

question: What is a primary treatment goal for clients with inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any family involvement
options.B: Maintaining the highest possible level of independence and comfort
options.C: Reversing the genetic mutation through intense physical exercise
options.D: Achieving a complete cure within six months of diagnosis

explanation: Since a cure is not available, goals focus on maximizing quality of life, function, and comfort. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h3)

question: What type of synovial joint allows you to move your shoulder and hip in almost every direction?

options.A: Ball-and-socket joint
options.B: Pivot joint
options.C: Hinge joint
options.D: Plane joint

explanation: Right on! Ball-and-socket joints (like your shoulder and hip) give you the widest range of motion in all directions. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T6#GNS121_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which test is best for looking at soft tissues like a torn knee ligament?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.C: Standard X-ray
options.D: Serum calcium blood test

explanation: MRI uses powerful magnets and radio waves to take clear pictures of soft tissues like ligaments and cartilage. X-rays are great for bones, but MRI wins for soft stuff! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h3)

question: What is a major part of helping a pregnant client make a practical birth plan?

options.A: Arranging transportation and identifying the place of delivery
options.B: Purchasing expensive imported toys for the nursery
options.C: Choosing the exact college the child will attend later
options.D: Deciding whether the mother will return to work in a week

explanation: A good birth plan solves logistics! Knowing how she will get to the hospital and exactly which health facility she is going to prevents dangerous delays during labor. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: Why do doctors perform a simple surgery called a hymenotomy for an imperforate hymen?

options.A: To create an opening in the membrane so trapped menstrual blood can drain
options.B: To treat an active bacterial vaginosis infection
options.C: To completely remove the entire vaginal canal
options.D: To reinforce weakened fascia against a developing cystocele

explanation: Spot on! Making a tiny cut in the blocked hymen relieves the pressure and lets the stored menstrual fluid empty out safely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h6)

question: Why did clinical research take a backseat to educational studies in early nursing history?

options.A: Nursing was heavily focused on following fixed hospital routines and administrative tasks
options.B: Physicians refused to let nurses learn how to read write research papers
options.C: There were no sick patients available in hospitals for students to study
options.D: Government laws strictly forbade nurses from observing patient symptoms

explanation: Great job thinking this through! Back then, nursing was driven more by strict hospital traditions and routines than by independent science, so administrative duties came first. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a major public health challenge for reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: Limited access to modern contraceptive methods
options.B: Universal excess availability of fertility treatments
options.C: High maternal mortality ratios in rural areas
options.D: High burden of sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Correct! Too many fertility treatments are definitely not the problem here—rather, it's struggling with basic maternal care access and preventable complications. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which baby position is required for a planned home delivery to be considered safe?

options.A: Transverse sideways lie
options.B: Any position the baby chooses
options.C: Breech bottom-first presentation
options.D: Cephalic head-first presentation

explanation: A head-first presentation is essential for a safe vaginal birth, especially outside of a hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h3)

question: How can long-term chronic workplace stress affect an employee physically?

options.A: It causes permanent hearing loss
options.B: It can contribute to high blood pressure and sleep problems
options.C: It leads to immediate skin burns from acids
options.D: It causes instant bone fractures

explanation: When psychological pressure stays high for too long, the body reacts physically—often showing up as high blood pressure, sleeplessness, and constant fatigue. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T5#GNS225_U7_T5_h6)

question: What is meant by a disease 'reservoir'?

options.A: Where the infectious agent normally lives and multiplies
options.B: The Department of Health data storage unit
options.C: A device used to measure patient body temperature
options.D: The specific medication given to kill a virus

explanation: Correct! A reservoir is the natural hiding and breeding place—whether in humans, animals, or soil—where a germ thrives and reproduces. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h3)

question: Which chemical in the body is mostly responsible for painful menstrual cramps?

options.A: Prostaglandins
options.B: Histamine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Prostaglandins make the muscles of the uterus squeeze tightly, which causes those familiar cramps. (That's also why anti-inflammatory painkillers help so much!) [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main job of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)?

options.A: Employing all newly graduated nurses directly
options.B: Setting international trade tariffs for medical supplies
options.C: Managing hospital budgets across all state capitals
options.D: Regulating standards of nursing education and practice

explanation: Correct! The NMCN sets the rules for nursing schools, issues our licenses, and keeps the profession standard and safe. [learn more](GST321_U8_T7#GST321_U8_T7_h4)

question: What is one of the main everyday duties of a community health nurse?

options.A: Assessing community needs and delivering health education
options.B: Managing national health insurance policies and budgets
options.C: Designing and constructing public water treatment plants
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgeries in local clinics

explanation: Community nurses spend a lot of time finding out what local health gaps exist and teaching the public how to stay well. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h6)

question: How should a nurse properly clean a medication vial septum before drawing up fluid?

options.A: Blow air heavily onto the rubber top to cool and clean it
options.B: Wipe the rubber top with an alcohol swab and allow it to dry
options.C: Wipe the top with a dry paper towel immediately before insertion
options.D: Run the entire glass bottle under hot tap water for one minute

explanation: Swabbing the septum with alcohol and letting it dry naturally reduces surface bacteria prior to needle insertion. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h5)

question: In the famous '4 Ts' mnemonic for the causes of postpartum haemorrhage, what does the very first 'T' stand for?

options.A: Traction
options.B: Tone
options.C: Tachycardia
options.D: Temperature

explanation: Tone refers to uterine atony (when the uterus doesn't contract well). This is actually the number one cause of PPH you will see in the wards! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h2)

question: What is the primary intervention for a patient after receiving a CT scan with intravenous contrast?

options.A: Encouraging generous fluid intake
options.B: Restricting all fluids for 12 hours
options.C: Keeping the patient flat on bed rest
options.D: Applying warm compresses to the IV site

explanation: Fluids help dilute and clear the iodinated contrast media through the renal system quickly, protecting the kidneys from injury. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is the separation of maternal and fetal blood inside the placenta important?

options.A: It prevents an immune reaction and protects against certain infections
options.B: It ensures that fetal blood pressure remains higher than maternal pressure
options.C: It allows blood cells to mix freely to boost the fetal immune system
options.D: It stops the mother from absorbing too much fetal waste

explanation: Keeping maternal and fetal circulations separate prevents the mother's immune system from attacking fetal cells and blocks many harmful pathogens from passing directly over. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h1)

question: What is the most critical check a nurse must do before giving penicillin for the first time?

options.A: Measuring the patient head circumference
options.B: Checking for a history of drug allergies
options.C: Evaluating the patient visual acuity score
options.D: Assessing the patient daily fluid intake

explanation: Safety first! Always check for allergies. A patient with a severe penicillin allergy can crash quickly from anaphylaxis if you miss this step. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which finding around a skeletal traction pin site should you report as a sign of infection?

options.A: Purulent drainage and foul odor
options.B: Dry crusting around the metal insertion point
options.C: Mild pinkness that fades within the first day
options.D: Small amounts of clear serosanguinous drainage

explanation: You got it! Pus and bad smells are telltale signs of bacteria at work. Light pinkness or dry crusting can just be normal early healing. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T9#GNS221_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why is it important to check expiration dates immediately upon receiving new supplies?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of each individual item
options.B: To determine how many nursing staff members are needed on duty
options.C: To decide which shelf in the storage cupboard looks the cleanest
options.D: To prevent accepting short-dated stock that might expire before use

explanation: Catching expired or near-expiry goods upon delivery allows the facility to return them before accepting responsibility for wasted items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why might a doctor perform a therapeutic lumbar puncture?

options.A: To remove a kidney stone from the ureter
options.B: To check the patient's blood glucose level
options.C: To lower high pressure inside the skull
options.D: To clear an airway blockage in the lungs

explanation: You got it! Removing extra fluid during the procedure helps relieve dangerous pressure inside the skull when there is a fluid buildup. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is a major safety worry for a patient who has lost feeling (protective sensation) in their arms or legs?

options.A: Rapid muscle hypertrophy
options.B: Excessive verbal outbursts
options.C: Sudden loss of hearing
options.D: Burns and pressure injuries

explanation: When patients can't feel hot, cold, or pressure, they won't pull away from a hot stove or shift their weight, leaving their skin wide open to quiet injuries and sores. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T22#GNS222_U3_T22_h3)

question: A patient asks if she can get pregnant before her first period returns after an abortion. What should you tell her?

options.A: No, menstruation must happen first to clear the path
options.B: No, the body is completely sterile for three months
options.C: Yes, because ovulation happens before the first period returns
options.D: Only if she had a surgical procedure instead of a medical one

explanation: Many patients are surprised by this! Ovulation happens first, meaning pregnancy is possible before that first post-abortion period shows up. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h2)

question: A patient's lab results show a high neutrophil count. What does this usually point to?

options.A: An active internal hemorrhage
options.B: A chronic viral illness
options.C: An acute bacterial infection
options.D: A severe lack of dietary iron

explanation: Neutrophils are your front-line soldiers against bacteria. When an acute bacterial infection strikes, their numbers shoot up rapidly to defend the body. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h3)

question: How does the vagus nerve normally affect the heart rate?

options.A: It stops ventricular contraction completely
options.B: It speeds up the heart rate
options.C: It slows down the heart rate
options.D: It strengthens the force of atrial contraction only

explanation: The vagus nerve is part of your body's 'rest and digest' system. When it acts on the heart, it helps calm things down and slows the heart rate. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h2)

question: When helping a Nigerian patient plan a healthy, balanced local diet, which food combination is best?

options.A: High-fat fried snacks consumed without any protein or vegetable source
options.B: Yam or cassava served with beans, fish, and green leafy vegetable soup
options.C: Strictly white refined sugar dissolved in large quantities of clean water
options.D: Imported processed canned foods supplemented with synthetic energy drinks

explanation: Wonderful! Combining local energy staples like yam or cassava with protein (beans, fish) and nutrient-rich green leaves gives a complete, culturally wonderful meal. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h6)

question: Which neurotransmitter is most directly linked to the brain's reward pathway and addiction?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Histamine
options.C: Serotonin
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Dopamine is the primary chemical messenger responsible for reinforcing rewarding experiences in the brain's reward center. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is the go-to medication for stopping and preventing seizures in severe preeclampsia?

options.A: Diazepam tablets
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Calcium gluconate
options.D: Hydralazine injection

explanation: You're doing great! Magnesium sulfate is the gold standard for managing eclamptic seizures and keeping mothers safe. A true midwifery essential! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h5)

question: What is the primary physical characteristic of a convulsion?

options.A: Sudden, involuntary muscle contractions
options.B: Complete relaxation of all skeletal muscles
options.C: Slow paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: A gradual loss of skin color

explanation: Convulsions involve rapid and repeated spasms of the skeletal muscles, leading to uncontrolled shaking. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T10#GNS222_U4_T10_h1)

question: A nurse manager checks if staff are following the correct aseptic technique during wound dressing changes. Which type of standard is being evaluated?

options.A: Structure standards
options.B: Outcome standards
options.C: Process standards
options.D: Legislative standards

explanation: Process standards look at the actual steps and actions nurses perform while carrying out patient care duties. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h2)

question: What do we call large cells with multiple nuclei formed when virus-infected cells fuse together?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Granulomas
options.C: Syncytia
options.D: Abscesses

explanation: Syncytia are giant multi-nucleated cells created when certain clever viruses trick neighboring cell membranes into melting together. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by community health nurses?

options.A: Poor road infrastructure and difficult geographical terrain
options.B: Inadequate medical supplies at primary healthcare centers
options.C: Unlimited availability of advanced surgical equipment in every village
options.D: Resistance from traditional or cultural belief systems

explanation: Community clinics rarely have unlimited advanced surgical equipment; resource scarcity is actually a major challenge in community practice. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h8)

question: Which health problem is most common among street populations due to a lack of clean drinking water and toilets?

options.A: Waterborne diarrheal diseases
options.B: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.C: Hereditary bleeding disorders
options.D: Congenital heart defects

explanation: Spot on. Without safe drinking water and good sanitation, tummy infections and diarrhea spread very easily. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T3#GNS225_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary function of the innermost layer, the tunica intima?

options.A: Anchoring major blood vessels securely to nearby skeletal bones
options.B: Supplying oxygenated blood directly to the thick outer muscle layers
options.C: Generating rhythmic electrical impulses to contract the vessel wall
options.D: Providing a frictionless endothelial surface for smooth blood flow

explanation: The tunica intima features a slick endothelial lining that reduces cellular friction and prevents unwanted clotting inside healthy vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why do we ask family planning clients to come back for follow-up visits?

options.A: To administer routine childhood immunizations
options.B: To conduct major diagnostic surgical procedures
options.C: To permanently discharge the client from care
options.D: To check on the client and offer ongoing support

explanation: Follow-up visits are all about seeing how the client is doing and giving them continuous support with their chosen contraceptive method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h1)

question: When should a primary health nurse initiate an upward referral for a psychiatric client?

options.A: As soon as the client's symptoms begin to improve on standard medication
options.B: Whenever the client misses a single routine clinic appointment
options.C: When the client develops severe psychosis or active suicidal ideation beyond local management
options.D: When the local clinic runs out of printed health education leaflets

explanation: If a patient's condition becomes too severe for the local clinic to safely handle—like active suicidal thoughts—it's time for an upward referral to specialists. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the main goal of program implementation in community health?

options.A: Putting planned health interventions into actual practice
options.B: Gathering baseline data before designing an intervention
options.C: Writing the initial budget proposal for a health project
options.D: Assessing the long-term impact of a finished program

explanation: Implementation is all about action! It means taking the written plan and making it happen out there in the community where people need care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h1)

question: What is the primary diagnostic test used to record the electrical activity of the brain in seizure disorders?

options.A: Complete blood count (CBC)
options.B: Lumbar puncture (LP)
options.C: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.D: Electroencephalogram (EEG)

explanation: An EEG measures and records the brain's electrical wave patterns to help identify abnormal activity. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h5)

question: What is a great way to keep a multisectoral team accountable and working well together?

options.A: Holding meetings only once every five years to review old records
options.B: Leaving each sector to work completely independently without reporting back
options.C: Establishing joint monitoring committees with representatives from all involved sectors
options.D: Allowing the health ministry to make all decisions without consulting others

explanation: Correct! Joint committees help everyone stay on the same page, track shared goals, and solve problems as a team. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h5)

question: Why is it important for nurses to know about local food taboos when caring for patients?

options.A: To determine the financial income of households in the village
options.B: To help identify hidden causes of malnutrition and poor health
options.C: To replace traditional beliefs with foreign culinary recipes
options.D: To enforce strict government fines against cultural practices

explanation: When people avoid certain foods because of taboos, they might miss out on vital nutrients. Spotting this helps you figure out the real reason behind nutritional deficiencies! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h1)

question: After identifying that a client's primary caregiver is exhausted, what is the best holistic nursing action?

options.A: Connect the family with local respite care and social work services
options.B: Tell the family member to stop worrying and sleep at the hospital
options.C: Ignore the finding since it is a family personal matter
options.D: Discharge the client immediately so the caregiver can rest

explanation: Collaborating with social workers to arrange respite care directly addresses caregiver burnout and supports safe home recovery. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h8)

question: How is oogenesis in females different from spermatogenesis in males?

options.A: Oogenesis continues at a rapid pace throughout old age
options.B: Oogenesis begins before birth and has a fixed supply of cells
options.C: Spermatogenesis produces fewer functional gametes over a lifetime
options.D: Spermatogenesis undergoes lengthy periods of meiotic arrest

explanation: You've got this! Unlike men who make new sperm all their lives, baby girls are born with all the eggs they will ever have. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why do we give nitroglycerin to a patient having chest pain from heart disease?

options.A: It dissolves existing blood clots inside the coronary arteries.

options.C: It permanently removes fatty plaque from the artery walls.
options.D: It dilates blood vessels to improve blood flow and lower heart workload.

explanation: Spot on! Nitroglycerin relaxes the blood vessels, widening the coronary arteries and making it much easier for the heart to pump. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T10#GNS111_U2_T10_h6)

question: Why is verifying pediatric weight before dosing medication from a standing order so critical?

options.A: Weight checks determine whether the child has received routine vaccinations
options.B: Children's drug doses depend heavily on their body weight to prevent toxicity
options.C: Weight is only used for billing purposes in government primary health centers
options.D: Standard adult doses are always safe for children if given with plenty of water

explanation: Unlike adults, pediatric medication safety relies on precise weight-based calculations to avoid dangerous overdosing or ineffective treatment. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h6)

question: What does internal validity measure in an experimental study?

options.A: Whether the study can be used in every hospital worldwide
options.B: How many nurses were hired to assist with data collection
options.C: Whether the treatment truly caused the observed outcome
options.D: How fast the patients answered the survey questions

explanation: Internal validity checks if outside factors ruined the experiment, ensuring the intervention itself made the difference. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h5)

question: What do Lewy bodies do inside the brain cells of someone with Parkinson's disease?

options.A: They protect neurons from inflammatory damage in the midbrain.
options.B: They accumulate inside nerve cells and disrupt normal cellular function.
options.C: They produce excessive amounts of dopamine to compensate for cell loss.
options.D: They repair damaged myelin sheaths around peripheral nerves.

explanation: Think of Lewy bodies like unwanted trash piling up inside the cell. These abnormal protein clumps build up, causing the nerve cells to get damaged and eventually die off. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T4#GNS222_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why must you carefully check the ceramic jar for cracks before pouring in boiling water?

options.A: To measure the exact volume capacity in milliliters
options.B: To remove leftover food particles from previous treatments
options.C: To ensure the inside is completely sterile for surgical use
options.D: To check for cracks that could leak or shatter from thermal shock

explanation: Safety first! Pouring boiling water into a damaged ceramic jar can cause it to shatter completely from thermal shock, risking severe burns. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T6#GNS212_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why are people with long-term HIV at a higher risk for heart disease?

options.A: Patients universally develop severe iron-deficiency anemia
options.B: Low red blood cell counts force the heart to beat faster
options.C: Persistent systemic inflammation damages blood vessels
options.D: The virus directly destroys heart muscle tissue daily

explanation: Ongoing immune activation keeps the body in a state of low-level inflammation, which over time can damage blood vessels and raise heart disease risk. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h5)

question: What is a research checklist mainly used for in nursing studies?

options.A: To schedule nursing staff shifts on the ward
options.B: To systematically record observations and data
options.C: To prescribe medication dosages to patients
options.D: To diagnose complex medical conditions

explanation: Think of a checklist as your organized guide! It gives you a structured way to observe and tick off items uniformly during a study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h1)

question: How often should you check and record the mother's pulse rate on the standard partograph?

options.A: Only after delivery
options.B: Once a day
options.C: Every 6 hours
options.D: Every 30 minutes

explanation: Checking the mother's pulse every half-hour helps you catch early signs of exhaustion, dehydration, or distress very quickly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h5)

question: What dangerous habit is a common form of erratic medication non-compliance?

options.A: Reporting mild nausea directly to the attending nurse
options.B: Consulting a pharmacist before changing a schedule
options.C: Storing prescription drugs in a cool, dry cupboard
options.D: Taking a double dose to makeup for a missed pill

explanation: Patients often try to compensate for a forgotten pill by taking two at the next scheduled time, which risks drug toxicity. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why is it so hard to listen to breath sounds with a regular stethoscope inside a flying aircraft?

options.A: Flight nurses are not permitted to use stethoscopes
options.B: Air pressure changes destroy the rubber tubing instantly
options.C: Patients stop breathing entirely when the engine starts
options.D: The high level of ambient engine noise masks lung sounds

explanation: Correct! Aircraft engines are very loud. Because the background noise makes auscultation tough, flight nurses rely heavily on monitors and capnography. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T14#GNS321_U2_T14_h7)

question: What is the minimum acceptable urine output for an adult patient that indicates adequate kidney perfusion?

options.B: 10.0 mL/kg/hour
options.C: 5.0 mL/kg/hour
options.D: 2.0 mL/kg/hour

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of rectovaginal fistula?

question: A nurse gives a patient pain medication. What is the best next step?

question: Why can assigning biological sex at birth based only on external genitals sometimes be tricky?

question: A patient asks how doctors will know for sure if a brain tumor is cancerous. What procedure gives the definitive diagnosis?

question: How do acquired bleeding problems differ from inherited conditions like hemophilia?

options.A: Acquired disorders develop later in life due to illnesses or deficiencies

question: What is the main goal of doing a nutritional check on a patient in primary health care?

question: A patient arrives with a neck injury and a crackling sensation felt under the skin. What does this sign suggest?

question: A patient with paraplegia sits in a wheelchair for hours without shifting weight. What skin problem is most likely to develop over their tailbone area?
